newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Tanzania, Kenya reject concessions by Burundi.
newsitem.headline: Tanzania, Kenya reject concessions by Burundi.

text.p: Tanzania and Kenya refused on Wednesday to ease sanctions against Burundi in return for Tutsi military leader Pierre Buyoya's lifting bans on parliament and political parties.
"The crucial condition...is the requirement that there has to be unconditional negotiations involving all parties to the conflict in Burundi," said Kenyan Foreign Minister Kalonzo Musyoka in Nairobi.
"I am not convinced much has happened in as much as the constitution remains suspended," he told reporters on Wednesday.

"As long as the constitution remains suspended it cannot be held there has been a change in attitude," added Musyoka, who said regional sanctions against Burundi were "a very painful but necessary step".
Asked about a call from Buyoya for a regional summit including a Burundi delegation, Musyoka said that depended on his seriousness to address crucial issues.
He said it would be pointless to have a regional summit if there was no way forward to resolve the Burundian problem.
Regional leaders fear Burundi may go the way of its northern neighbour Rwanda where up to an estimated one million people were killed in genocide and three months of civil war in 1994.

Like Musyoka, the Tanzanian foreign ministry said earlier that Buyoya had failed to act on the most important demand by regional African leaders: unconditional negotiations with all parties to the conflict both inside and outside Burundi.

It said Buyoya's concessions lacked detail and fell short of demands made at regional summits in Arusha, northern Tanzania, on June 25 and June 31 for talks on power-sharing with the Hutu National Council for the Defence of Democracy (CNDD).
Buyoya, who seized power from Hutu President Sylvestre Ntibantunganya in a July 25 coup by the Tutsi-dominated army, last Friday lifted bans on political parties and parliament.
But he says he cannot open unconditional negotiations with Hutu rebels and demands they first lay down their weapons.
